h1: Khaolak Merlin Resort — a beachfront garden resort made for families in Khao Lak
intro: Khao Lak is a far quieter coast than Phuket or Krabi — made for travellers who want to escape the crowds and actually fall asleep to the waves. Khaolak Merlin Resort is a large 4-star resort on about 190m of Khao Lak beach, set in more than 15 acres of tropical gardens. Its real draw is the four pools, with a waterslide and a separate kids' pool, which make it a firm favourite with families. From approx. THB 2,500/night. Scored 8.9 from 1,036 Booking.com reviews.

body.html: Khaolak Merlin Resort has been open since 2003 and had a major renovation in 2020. It's a large resort of around 200 rooms, spread across more than 15 acres of tropical gardens on the southern stretch of Khao Lak beach in Lam Kaen. The thing guests mention most is how lush and shaded the gardens are — tall trees throughout, so much so that many say it feels like staying in the middle of a jungle, waking up to birdsong instead of traffic.

There's a wide spread of room types, starting with the Superior at 37 sqm and the Deluxe at 44 sqm, both with wood furniture and a balcony onto the gardens. Step up and you get the Pool Access rooms you can walk straight into the pool from your terrace (Garden Pool Access at 39 sqm, Waterfall Pool Access at 46 sqm). For bigger families there's the One Bedroom Pool Villa (131 sqm) and the Two Bedroom Pool Villa (168 sqm) with a private pool. Most guests praise how clean the rooms are and how spacious they feel for the price.
"We came with two kids — they spent the whole day on the waterslide and wouldn't get out, while we sipped coffee in the shade. For a family trip to Khao Lak this place just works."

The heart of the place is its four pools, with a waterslide and a separate kids' pool — the main reason families with young children pick it. Beyond that there's a private beach of around 190m, a spa, a tennis court, a gym, and two restaurants: Tropical Garden serves all day, including the breakfast buffet, while Veranda focuses on seafood and grills in the evening. Because the grounds are so large, the resort never feels crowded despite the number of rooms.

The honest trade-offs are around dining choice and some service points. A fair number of reviews note that food options inside the resort are limited and the beachfront restaurant isn't as strong as it could be, and pool-bar service can be slow at busy times. Because it's a big resort on wide grounds, some rooms are a fair walk from the beach and lobby. The location is southern Khao Lak, about 50 minutes from Phuket Airport (HKT) — peaceful, but with few restaurants and shops outside the resort.

In short, Khaolak Merlin Resort is best for families and anyone after a beachfront resort in leafy gardens at an affordable price, rather than a small design-led boutique. Rates start from approx. THB 2,500/night for a Superior in low season, rising to THB 6,000–8,000+ for Pool Access rooms and Pool Villas in high season. It scores 8.9 from 1,036 Booking.com reviews and 4.5 on TripAdvisor (ranked #11 of 85 hotels in Khao Lak) — numbers that reflect a long, steady popularity.

A tip from reading the reviews: if you're travelling with kids, ask for a room near the waterslide pool or in the Pool Access cluster — it's far more convenient. If you want to be close to the sea, request a beach-side zone when you book. In high season (November–April), book at least a month ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first.

honestSummary: Khaolak Merlin Resort is best for families and travellers after a beachfront resort in leafy gardens at an affordable price — lots of pools with a waterslide and a kids' pool, on wide, quiet grounds. But accept that dining choice inside the resort is limited, it's a way from town and the airport, and it's a big resort where some rooms are a walk from the beach.
honestChecks: If you want a small, design-led boutique with high privacy — this is a large family resort that gets lively around the pools → consider Casa de la Flora or The Sarojin in this roundup instead.
If you plan to eat every meal at the resort — restaurant choice is limited and the beach restaurant isn't a standout → plan to eat out in Khao Lak sometimes, or rent a car.

If you're travelling with young kids and want convenience — the grounds are wide and some rooms are far from the pools and beach → request a room near the waterslide pool or the Pool Access cluster when you book.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Khaolak Merlin Resort, Khao Lak, Phang Nga

faq.q: Where is Khaolak Merlin Resort and how do I get there?
faq.a: Khaolak Merlin Resort is on Phetkasem Road in Lam Kaen, Thai Mueang district, Phang Nga Province, on the southern stretch of Khao Lak beach. It's about 50 minutes by car from Phuket Airport (HKT), around 10 minutes from Thap Lamu pier (for the Similans), and 15 minutes from Bang Niang Beach. The resort can arrange an airport transfer — request it when you book.

faq.q: How much does Khaolak Merlin Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 2,500/night for a Superior (37 sqm). From there you can step up to a Deluxe (44 sqm), Garden or Waterfall Pool Access rooms (walk straight into the pool), and One- or Two-Bedroom Pool Villas (131–168 sqm) with a private pool. High-season rates climb, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Khaolak Merlin Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for families with young children, thanks to its four pools, waterslide and kids' pool, and wide, shaded gardens. It suits travellers who want a quiet beachfront resort at an affordable price, rather than a small design-led boutique.

faq.q: What pools and facilities does Khaolak Merlin Resort have?
faq.a: There are four outdoor pools, including a waterslide and a separate kids' pool, plus a private beach of around 190m, a spa, a tennis court, a gym, and two restaurants (Tropical Garden serving all day, and Veranda for seafood and grills in the evening).

faq.q: What is the food like at Khaolak Merlin Resort?
faq.a: There are two restaurants and a breakfast buffet at Tropical Garden. Some reviews note that dining choice inside the resort is limited and the beach restaurant isn't a standout. It's worth eating out in Khao Lak or Bang Niang sometimes for a change of scene.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and can I cancel?
faq.a: In high season (November–April), book at least a month ahead, especially for Pool Access rooms or Pool Villas. Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — pick that first if your plans aren't firm, then compare prices across a few sites before confirming.
